messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** the freezing point of pure water is only slightly above the standard 0 °C reference.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition (ΔV ≈ –9 × 10⁻⁶ m³ mol⁻¹ and ΔS ≈ 1.8 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ near 0 °C) gives a slope of roughly –7 × 10⁻³ K kPa⁻¹.  
From 101.3 kPa down to 10 kPa the pressure drops by 91.3 kPa, raising the melting temperature by about:

\[
\Delta T \approx 91.3\;\text{kPa}\times 7\times10^{-3}\;\frac{\text{K}}{\text{kPa}}\approx +0.64\;\text{K}
\]

So the freezing point at 10 kPa is approximately **+0.6 °C** (about 0.65 °C).  

(For comparison, the boiling point at this pressure is ~45 °C.)

Let's recall: At 1 atm (101.325 kPa), freezing point is 0°C. As pressure decreases, freezing point increases? Actually for water, freezing point decreases with increasing pressure (negative slope). So at lower pressure, freezing point is higher? Wait, water has negative Clapeyron slope: dT/dP = ΔV/ΔS. For melting, ΔV = V_liquid - V_solid > 0, so dT/dP positive? Actually for water, solid has lower volume than liquid, so ΔV negative, so dT/dP negative. So as pressure increases, freezing point decreases. So at lower pressure, freezing point increases. So at 10 kPa (< 101.3 kPa), freezing point should be slightly above 0°C. How much? The slope near 1 atm is about -0.0072 K/kPa? Actually dT/dP ~ -0.0072 K/kPa? That would mean at 10 kPa difference of 91.3 kPa from 101.3, change ~ -0.66 K? Wait sign: dT/dP negative means increase in pressure lowers T. So at lower pressure, T higher. So at 10 kPa, T ~ 0°C + (101.3-10)*0.0072 ≈ 0 + 91.3*0.0072 ≈ 0.657°C. So freezing point ~ +0.66°C. But check actual values: At 10 kPa, freezing point ~ 0.65°C. So answer: ~0.65°C.
